All elements should meet or exceed the following criteria: SCOPE OF WORK Statement of Work: Biotechnology Policy Advocacy: Government Engagement and Academic Outreach Program SCOPE Conduct three workshops at a selected venue and three site visits to an agricultural biotechnology research center or a feed/food plant, led by international and domestic experts holding relevant academic credentials in biotechnology, agricultural sciences, biological sciences, or a closely related field. These activities will advocate against proposed anti-biotechnology legislation and policies in Colombia and encourage wider understanding, acceptance, and adoption of biotechnology among key stakeholder groups. PURPOSE Since 2022, Colombia has remained open to the adoption of genetically engineered (GE)-derived commodities and other innovative technologies and has implemented various regulations facilitating GE cultivation and acceptance. Nevertheless, anti-biotechnology influences risk undoing decades of progress in this space and threaten U.S. market access of key GE commodities to the Colombian market. While technical-level government officials favor biotechnology adoption, various activist groups have

PURPOSE Since 2022, Colombia has remained open to the adoption of genetically engineered (GE)-derived commodities and other innovative technologies and has implemented various regulations facilitating GE cultivation and acceptance. Nevertheless, anti-biotechnology influences risk undoing decades of progress in this space and threaten U.S. market access of key GE commodities to the Colombian market. While technical-level government officials favor biotechnology adoption, various activist groups have successfully lobbied certain legislators to reject the science and the concept of biotechnology in general. Over six consecutive legislative years beginning in Page 3 of 6 July 2020, bills aimed at establishing “transgenic-free” municipalities, protecting farmers’ rights to save, reuse, and commercialize their seeds, and a GE seed ban have all been introduced in Congress. On November 2, 2023, Colombia’s Constitutional Court upheld a 2022 law mandating that the government take actions to protect indigenous land and native seeds and avoid risks derived from the release of living modified organisms from biotechnology processes. While technical-level government officials favor biotechnology adoption, various activist groups have successfully lobbied certain legislators to reject the science and the concept of biotechnology in general. Over six consecutive legislative years beginning in Page 3 of 6 July 2020, bills aimed at establishing “transgenic-free” municipalities, protecting farmers’ rights to save, reuse, and commercialize their seeds, and a GE seed ban have all been introduced in Congress. On November 2, 2023, Colombia’s Constitutional Court upheld a 2022 law mandating that the government take actions to protect indigenous land and native seeds and avoid risks derived from the release of living modified organisms from biotechnology processes. In June 2026, the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development published its legal review of the Court’s ruling and stated that Colombia will need to integrate new cultural impact assessments into the GE approval process. submission.text: . This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; offers are being requested, and a written solicitation will not be issued. The solicitation number is 19GV1026Q0015 and is issued as a Request for Quotation. The solicitation/contract includes all applicable provisions and clauses in effect. The U.S. Government intends to award a contract/purchase order to the responsible company submitting an acceptable offer at the lowest price. We intend to award a contract/purchase order based on initial quotations, without holding discussions, although we may hold discussions with companies in the competitive range if there is a need to do so. The deadline for submitting offers is Tuesday, September 8, 2026, at 16:00 UTC + 00:00. No quotation will be accepted after this time. Proposals must be in English and incomplete proposals will not be accepted. To ensure vendors get a clear understanding of the services and consumables required under the expected contract, the embassy will be conducting guided visits for equipment verification on Thursday, August 13, 2026 between 9:00 AM and 3:00 PM local time in Conakry, Guinea. Your offer must be addressed to the Contracting Officer and submitted electronically to ConakryProc@state.gov. It is important to make sure the submission is made in a specific

d format; in MS-Word 2007/2010 or MS-Excel 2007/2010 or Adobe Acrobat (pdf) file format. The file size must not exceed 30MB. If the file size should exceed 30MB, the submission must be made in separate files and attached to separate emails with less than 30MB each. Offer packages must consist of two distinct but not necessarily exclusive parts. Part A, the financial offer, must be consistent with section 1 (Pricing) and must disclose without ambiguity, all costs associated with the performance of the services and the provision of the consumables required under the expected contract. Hidden or undisclosed costs will not be accepted after the deadline and any award made on the basis of undisclosed costs will be subject to withdrawal or cancellation. Part B, the technical offer, must clearly and fully address the requirements in the statement of work and all other requirements in this solicitation. Should you have questions please contact Fama Marah (+224 629 000 534) via email to marahf@state.gov with cc to ConakryProc@state.gov. PURPOSE QUALITY ASSURANCE SURVEILLANCE PLAN (QASP) FOR NIWDC EWD SUPPORT SERVICES IDIQ This Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP) is a Government developed and applied document used to make sure that systematic quality assurance methods are used in the administration of the Performance Based Service Contract (PBSC) standards included in this contract. The intent is to ensure that the Contractor performs in accordance with performance metrics set forth in the contract documents, that the Government receives the quality of services called for in the contract, and that the Government only pays for the acceptable level of services received. The QASP ensures t

by the PWS in a timely, accurate, and complete fashion 2. AUTHORITY Authority for issuance of this QASP is provided under the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 52.212-4 “CONTRACT TERMS AND CONDITIONS – COMMERCIAL ITEMS (OCT 2003), paragraph (b), which provides for inspections and acceptance of the articles, services, and documentation called for in task orders to be accomplished by the Contracting Officer or his duly authorized representative. 3. SCOPE The Contractor, and not the Government, is responsible for management and quality control actions necessary to meet the quality standards set forth by the contract. The Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP) has been put in place to provide Government surveillance oversight of the Contractor’s quality control efforts to ensure that they are timely, effective and are delivering the results specified in the contract. The QASP is not a part of the contract nor is it intended to duplicate the Contractor’s Management Plan. The Government may provide the Contractor with an information copy of the QASP as an attachment to the solicitation to support the Contractor’s efforts in developing its plan for maintaining the levels of quality anticipated to be delivered under the terms of the contract. 4. The purpose of this RFI is to gather industry input on how cloud-native COTS solutions, configurations, standard integrations and supporting services can best meet NATO’s needs. 2. Responses will assist in: x Identifying potential solutions that could deliver the target outcomes outlined in the Epic-Outcome Matrix (Annex B: Part 2) and their indicative costs; x Identifying solutions that are proven and deployed in public procurement settings; x Validating, challenging or refining the current planning assumptions and requirements; x Identifying security, hosting, data resi dency, supplier-access, records-management and accreditation considerations; and, x Identifying key risks, constr aints and alternative packaging, phasing or acquisition options that NCIA and relevant NATO stakeholders should consider in shaping any future solicitation. C. Background 1. NATO is pursuing digital transformation. Within this context, the digital enablement of sourcing and procurement processes has become a critical focus. ABOUT CAPACITY BUILDING Within CSD, Capacity Building (CB) serves as CISA’s enterprise cybersecurity services management arm for national stakeholders and the lead for Federal enterprise cybersecurity governance. CB enables its customers to manage cybersecurity risk by building their capacity to implement effective cybersecurity policies, tools, and procedures. CB helps stakeholders better manage cybersecurity risk by 1) Defining expectations for stakeholder cybersecurity; 2) Leading implementation and enforcement of cybersecurity requirements; 3) Managing CISA’s cybersecurity services portfolio; 4) Building capacity; and 5) Enhancing collective defense and readiness. 1.1.1. Confirm production readiness prior to the scheduled cutover. EHRVIP Readiness The contractor shall support the project activities required for EHRVIP (EHR-Specific, Veteran-Focused, Integration Process) readiness with the VA EHRM program and Oracle Health teams, including: Quality assurance readiness activities. Verification of interface readiness. Support preparation of the Go Memo. Address outstanding technical issues and dependencies required for production implementation. Production Cutover and Go-Live The contractor shall provide technical support for the scheduled production implementation. Activities shall include: Participate in production cutover activities with the VA EHRM program and Oracle Health. Validate interface connectivity and functionality following deployment. deliverables_scope.text: ffairs (VA) is seeking information from qualified contractors regarding the continued development, testing, implementation, Go-Live support, and post-Go-Live support for enhancements to the Health Information and Gateway Exchange (HINGE) interface with Oracle Health. The requested period of performance is September 24, 2026, through April 19, 2027, for a total of seven months. This period is intended to support completion of the remaining interface development activities through the planned Oracle Health production Go-Live for the Wisconsin market on January 16, 2027, followed by post-Go-Live stabilization and support. Please see below DRAFT Statement of Work. Responses: Please submit the below requested information by 1:00PM EDT on Thursday, August 20th via email to Ryan Allen, Contract Specialist at Ryan.Allen@va.gov, and Kawana Tyler-Simms, Contract Specialist at Kawana.Tyler-Simms@va.gov. Activities shall include: Monitor and troubleshoot production interface issues. Investigate issues not identified during testing. Correct interface defects within the contractor's scope. Coordinate with VA, HINGE, and Oracle Health personnel. Document production issues and resolutions. Support stabilization of the interface following Go-Live. 3.8. Cybersecurity and ATO Support The contractor shall provide cybersecurity project management and support for continuous monitoring and maintenance of the applicable Authority to Operate (ATO) requirements associated with the HINGE interface.
